title: Probe staleness eviction policy and adaptive readiness SLO guard
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: In multi-region deployments the autoscaler and readiness gates can react to stale or duplicated probe signals produced during transient network partitions, kubelet restarts, or probe proxying through regional gateways. Those stale signals cause oscillation (scale thrash), unnecessary load-shedding, and accidental circuit trips that violate our latency/availability SLOs.

Goal: Implement a lightweight probe-staleness detection and eviction policy plus an adaptive readiness SLO guard layer that reduces stale-signal influence on autoscaling and circuit-breakers while preserving fast failover behavior. The change must be safe to rollout (config flags, canary by region) and observable (metrics, dashboards, and alert thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Staleness detection: probes include a monotonic probe_id and last_seen timestamp; stale entries (no fresh probe_id within threshold) are evicted from probe cache
Reduction in noise: synthetic canary shows >= 90% reduction in stale probe-driven readiness flips during network partition simulation
Autoscaler stability: canary region shows >= 60% reduction in scale-up/scale-down oscillations (measured as scale events per hour) during burst tests
SLO preservation: no increase in 99th tail latency and error rate for tested routes during canary rollout; rollback triggers if 99th latency regresses by >10%
Operational controls: feature gated with runtime flag, toggleable per-region and per-service via console/route config
Observability: Grafana dashboard with probe_evictions, probe_staleness_score, readiness_eval_skips, autoscale_event_rate and a synthetic job measuring flapping rate
tasks: Draft design doc describing probe_id format, staleness scoring, and eviction window (link in links)
Add probe_id and last_seen propagation in probe agent (kubelet proxy / regional gateway) and update probe ingestion schema
Implement in-memory probe cache eviction with exponential backoff for re-trust
Update readiness evaluator to consult staleness score and optionally skip/soft-fail ready->not-ready transitions
Create canary plan: enable in staging, then one region, monitor for 72h, then expand
Load/chaos tests: partition simulation, kubelet restart, gateway failover; run regression harness
Rollout runbook and rollback plan; QA signoff and SRE review
comments: 2025-11-03 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after postmortem of 2025-10-28 multi-region flapping incident. Initial idea: detect stale probe frames and reduce their weight in readiness scoring.
2025-11-04 - Marco Li: Spike completed. Prototype uses probe_id + last_seen and a lightweight LRU cache. Observed stale frames when gateway replays old probes during failover.
2025-11-06 - SRE (Jamal Ortiz): Suggest adding a 'grace re-trust' window to avoid false evictions for temporarily delayed probes. Also request an opt-out for legacy services.
2025-11-08 - Design review (Priya Nair): UX for regional toggle in Console approved; recommend labeling "probe-trust" controls under 'Reliability' tab.
2025-11-10 - Marco Li: Implemented initial eviction logic in a feature branch. Metrics wired to test Grafana dashboard. Running partition chaos in staging now.
decision_log: Use probe_id + last_seen rather than full hash comparison to keep probe frames small and network-friendly.
Eviction policy: soft-evict (mark stale) after T_stale, hard-evict after 3*T_stale. T_stale default 12s but configurable per-service.

Readiness behavior: prefer soft-fail (downgrade to 'degraded' state) instead of immediate NotReady to avoid autoscaler thrash. Circuit-breaker will be able to trigger if degradation persists beyond window.
Regional trust: local-region probe sources are weighted higher; cross-region probe proxying can be marked with 'proxied=true' and have stricter staleness thresholds.
Telemetry: emit detailed histograms for staleness_age and eviction_reason to support later tuning.
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased latency or SLO violations, flip feature flag off per-region (Console toggle) which disables staleness eviction and reverts readiness evaluator to previous behavior. If metrics pipeline introduced issues, rollback the ingestion schema change and fallback to ingesting only last_seen timestamps.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive eviction reduces noise but can mask legitimate delayed probes, which may delay failover. To balance this we use soft-degrade windows and conservative defaults with runtime knobs. Future work: integrate token-aware admission so high-value requests bypass degraded routing, and explore ML-based staleness scoring. Also coordinate with Dedicated capacity team's autoscaler to ensure committed pools don't scale down due to transient probe staleness.
